answer_text: Dispersion is the phenomenon in which white light separates into its seven colours when it passes through a transparent medium such as a glass prism. Each colour travels at a slightly different speed in glass, so each has a different refractive index. Violet, with the smallest wavelength, is slowed the most and is bent towards the base through the largest angle. Red is bent the least. The colours therefore emerge as a spectrum from violet to red.
